Strategic read on round 1: my unit cost is 50.9, so I break even only at a price of 51+. A price of 45 by seller_1 is below my cost — even if they were profitable it's a weak/expensive position for us to fight over.

My deliberate choice: I will NOT undercut the 45 bid (not to 44, not to tie at 45). Both options are losses for me: tying would hand me 30 units at −6.9 each (−207 total), undercutting to 44 would lock in 60 units at −6.9 each (−414) and trigger exactly the undercut I expect them to take next. A firm can't profitably "chase" a sub-cost price floor.

Today I'm going to let seller_1 (and any future challengers) absorb the low bid at no cost to me, and I will contest the market on terms where my cost structure can support a price above 51. This maximizes total expected profit across the whole game. Next rounds, I'll reassess their willingness to raise prices before I enter the price floor.

I'll hold my floor at 48 (just above cost, non-binding) and stay out of the 45-price contest until the market clears my cost — the moment someone bids 49+, I will undercut to 48 and capture the whole market at +0.6 per unit (36 for 60 units). Profit this round: 0 (I earn nothing while they hold 45), but I avoid sinking money into a war I can't win and preserve the opportunity to be the highest-margin winner when the leader finally retreats.
